description: [DIST-CI-WIN-VSIX] Feature chunks of the VS Code end-to-end suite. Each chunk is one Windows CI job running a slice of the SAME suite through the real LSP inside the real extension host. Single source of truth: the Makefile (_test-vsix-win), the CI matrix, and the coverage guard all read this file. Consumed via tools/vsix/vsix-test-chunks.mjs.

shared.description: Prepended to every chunk. Asserts the bundled host + sidecars were staged before the extension host started, so a staging regression fails as itself instead of as a wall of LSP timeouts.

lifecycle.description: Activation, configuration, bundled binary/sidecar resolution, client lifecycle and restart, cross-cutting command workflows.

lsp.description: C# language intelligence over the real LSP: completion, hover, diagnostics, document symbols, folding, selection ranges, code actions, document sync, client lifecycle.

fsharp.description: F# is a first-class citizen, so its whole LSP surface is gated on Windows: navigation, intelligence, syntax, diagnostics, code fixes, hierarchy, workspace symbol.

debug.description: Debugging end to end (launch/attach config resolution, netcoredbg adapter factory, sharplsp.debugProgram against real projects) plus Test Explorer discovery/run/debug and the test-status CodeLens.

profiler.description: Profiling end to end (dotnet-trace sessions, live counters, memory dumps, .nettrace conversion, profiler webviews) plus FSI, build, output filtering and hot reload.

explorer.description: Solution Explorer tree, reactive sort/state signals, tooltips and reveal, the full context-menu surface, and the project-dependency watcher.

packages.description: Scaffolding (create solution/project) and the NuGet surface: browser panel, search/add/update/restore commands, and real .csproj dependency edits.

excluded.description: Runs on Ubuntu (test-vsix) only. Each suite clones and restores a pinned real repository before cold-loading its solution, which adds ~10-15 minutes per suite; the Windows gate proves the feature surface, not third-party repo ingestion.
